A model of separated capabilities

The Nine Bodies of Authority

Version 8 · Words from the Expanded edition (30 pages, 26 October 2026)

Action, authorisation and account across nine connected domains, with three ways to position them.

Every function in society answers three different questions: what is being done, whether it may be done, and what account is kept of it. The Nine Bodies of Authority gives each question its own position and repeats that pattern across nine domains, from government to everyday cultural life. The model classifies functions, not institutions. One organisation can hold several positions, and one person can move between them in a single day, but the positions never merge.

The model has two parts. Parts I to V set out the nine bodies: the three positions, the principle that keeps them apart, the nine domains, and the loop that connects them, demonstrated through two worked cases. Part VI places the bodies on a three-bit cube that records how open each body is to the person in front of it, and sets out three routes through that cube. Part VII records what is settled, how the model was built, and its terms.

Embodied agentEnacts and submitsResponds and requests. What is being proposed, attempted or carried out?
Authoritative bodyApproves or deniesMay this proceed under the requirements that apply?
Authoritative agentRecords and reviewsReturns the account. What happened, under what conditions, and how does it compare?
Part I

The three positions

PositionCapabilityThe question it answers
Embodied agentEnacts and submits; responds and requestsWhat is being proposed, attempted or carried out?
Authoritative bodyApproves or deniesMay this proceed under the requirements that apply?
Authoritative agentRecords and reviews, returning an accountWhat happened, under what conditions, and how does it compare?

An embodied agent enacts or requests. An authoritative body approves or denies. An authoritative agent records and reviews. The returned account decides what happens next.

An action shows that something happened. An approval shows that a designated body allowed it. A reviewed account shows the conditions, the process and the consequences. None of the three stands in for another. An approved action can still be carried out badly, and a well-executed action can still have been wrongly approved.

Four failures, four remedies

This is what makes responsibility locatable. When an operation fails, the model separates four failures: an inadequate proposal, an unjustified approval, poor execution, and an incomplete or misleading account. They can occur together, but each one demands its own remedy.

FailureWhere it sitsIts remedy
An inadequate proposalEmbodied agentA better request
An unjustified approvalAuthoritative bodyCorrection at the gate
Poor executionEmbodied agentCorrection of the work
An incomplete or misleading accountAuthoritative agentCorrection of the record

The circuit

The three positions form a circuit, and the circuit has two movements.

The first is submission. The embodied agent enacts and submits: it carries something into effect and puts it forward for decision. Enact is chosen over act deliberately. To act is to perform; to enact is to give something formal effect, as a law is enacted or an authorised order carried out. The authoritative body approves or denies. The authoritative agent records and reviews that decision and returns the account to the embodied agent.

The second is the continuing loop. Holding the returned account, the embodied agent now responds and requests: it answers what came back and asks for what comes next. The authoritative body approves or denies again, the authoritative agent records and reviews again, and the account comes back again. The account belongs to the agent who receives it, to use, to influence and to decide upon.

The authoritative agent

The third position is separate from the authoritative body, yet belongs to it: it is the body’s self-examination. It never approves or denies, and it never acts. It consolidates an account of what the body has done, reviews that account against the conditions around it and against baseline comparisons, and returns a recorded assessment that informs the next request and the next decision.

The embodied agent is a position, not a headcount: a whole workforce can occupy it. The account does not wait for the action to finish. Existing records inform a request before it is made, an approval while it is considered, and an intervention while it runs. A body of authority is the whole triad, not just its approving position.

Part II

Separation of capabilities

The model begins with concentrated power. A body that can watch people, interpret what it sees and act against them, all under one roof, answers to no one.

Picture a county police force. Its officers patrol and respond in person, among the people they serve. Now give the same office ten thousand live camera feeds from the suburb it patrols, an analytic system to read them, and the authority to dispatch on whatever that system flags. The officers no longer meet the public on equal terms. They watch it from a room. That is the arrangement the model refuses.

The three capabilities are therefore held apart. Surveillance keeps the record, intelligence weighs information and authorises operations, and enforcement carries them out. They cooperate case by case, under authorisation that is itself recorded and reviewable. Every handoff runs through a defined channel: who may request footage, for what purpose, who approves the request, what analysis is permitted, what is logged, and who may challenge it. The live monitoring of a whole population never sits in the hands of the people who make arrests.

Cooperation never grants access. Taking part in a shared process gives no position the infrastructure, resources or powers of another.

Every triad is built by the same test: which capabilities must never be held together? Each position is defined as much by what it cannot do as by what it does. The three positions are distinct and cooperating. None is subordinate to another and none dominates.

No body rules another

No triad dominates another. Within each triad the authoritative body decides whether an action proceeds, which is power over that action and never power over the other bodies. Intelligence decides operations in body 3 exactly as the judicial body decides applications in body 2.

Intelligence shows why the rule matters most where power gathers most. It is the apex of body 3, the point where information is fed up to the directors and heads who decide. Because it decides, it holds neither the cameras nor the hands. Surveillance keeps the record, enforcement keeps the field, intelligence keeps the decision, and each weighs against the other two like the arms of a balance.

Auditorial

Auditorial is the one term the model coins. It names a power every person holds simply by existing: the power to scrutinise institutions, individually and collectively, without holding any of their other powers. Through it the public, as its own collective, watches everything else. The auditorial position records and reviews authorised material, procedures and outcomes. It cannot argue, judge, enforce, confine or surveil. However strong its findings, it never turns them into a ruling or an arrest by its own hand.

What it produces

Its output is a report: a declared method, an analysis of the data, and a cross-examination of the accounts, written within the bounds and requirements a judicial ruling sets after legal argument. Cross-examination here means testing accounts against one another inside the report, not advocacy in a courtroom. The report is a bounded assessment others act upon, and its findings stay open to challenge.

How a finding becomes action

Auditorial has no hands, so its findings travel through the chain that already exists. Whether a flagged matter is acted on rests on precedent, set by the judicial body in earlier cases. Precedent rests on legislation and on the legal argument that interprets it. Both rest on the constitutional enactment of government, which rests on what the public wants, and the whole national order sits within international law and the diplomatic relations that carry it. A finding enters that chain as a concern. The chain decides the outcome, and any order or enforcement that follows belongs to the body authorised to give it.

Bounded corruption

That limit is what bounds its capacity for corruption. A position that cannot argue, judge, enforce, confine or surveil cannot convert what it finds into power. Legal and judicial power shape how auditorial scrutiny is conducted, and auditorial scrutiny holds legal and judicial power to account.

Auditorial inspects how power was used. It does not watch private life. The line runs between evidence of institutional conduct, which it examines, and the private lives of people, which it never enters. Holding that line keeps public scrutiny from becoming universal surveillance.

Function, not institution

Classification follows the activity being performed, not the organisation performing it. A bank deciding whether to extend a loan occupies the commercial position. The same bank maintaining and reviewing the account of balances, obligations and repayments occupies the financial position. The two happen in one building, often at one desk, and they remain two functions. A journalist who makes entertainment is creating content at that moment, and a creator who investigates a public claim is doing journalism at that moment.

Part III

The nine bodies

The three positions repeat across nine domains. Each domain is a complete body of authority. Every name is held to one or two words, so the names stay comparable across the table.

approve or deny		Authoritative agent

3Enforcement: requests operational permission and carries out authorised interventionsIntelligence: assesses information and approves or denies proposed operationsSurveillance: records and reviews observations through separately controlled monitoring infrastructure
4Development logistics: designs, plans, builds, maintains, and moves people and goodsCivic welfare: approves or denies proposals against community requirementsProperty stewardship: records and reviews ownership, tenure, possessions and asset responsibilities

6Medical: provides treatment, care, and health and fitness interventionsScientific: approves or denies proposals against established scientific requirementsNutritional provision: records and reviews food production, preparation, consumption and requirements

How each body is drawn

1

Governmental, constitutional, diplomatic

Governmental agents turn public concern into proposals and administer what is approved, including military defence.

The constitutional body tests every proposal against the foundational distribution of powers and protections, in the manner of a supreme court. Its permission is not endorsement: a constitutional approval says a proposal is lawful, not that it is wise. A constitution is something a government must adhere to and something a people can amend, and amendment is a process of its own: public agreement does not rewrite a constitution automatically.

Diplomatic agents hold the account of relationships, commitments and conditions beyond the border. They are the nation’s representatives and delegates, and each carries the whole authority in a single person. That is what gives the position its review. The diplomat consolidates an account of the nation represented, compares it against the laws, decisions and circumstances of other nations and against the external limits, pressures and baseline comparisons the nation operates within, and returns that assessment home. The review faces outward in order to inform the inside.

2

Legal, judicial, auditorial

Legal agents build arguments, file applications and answer decisions. The judicial body rules on them, and its rulings set the precedent later cases rely on. Auditorial records the evidence, procedure, reasoning and outcome, and returns that account to everyone with standing to question it.

3

Enforcement, intelligence, surveillance

Enforcement requests operations and carries them out in the world. Its agents are the public face of the triad: the officers a person calls, meets and reports to.

Intelligence assesses information and decides whether each operation proceeds. It is the knowledge architecture of the triad: the agencies, analysts and systems in which information is gathered, weighed and held, and the heads who decide on it. It is where this triad’s decisions are made, never its eyes or its hands.

Surveillance holds the observational record on infrastructure controlled separately from both.

4

Development logistics, civic welfare, property stewardship

Development logistics covers architecture, design, planning, construction, maintenance and the movement of people and goods. Transport is one expression of it, and its wider function is organising change in the material world. Planning proposals belong here, with the agents who draw and submit them.

Civic welfare approves or denies proposals against community requirements such as access, disruption and the needs of affected residents, and against the health of the population the work touches. Setting district rules is an authorising act and sits here.

Property stewardship holds the account of land, buildings, tenure, district and location records, possessions, ownership claims, use rights and asset condition. It records who owns, claims, occupies or manages what, and checks compliance with the rules civic welfare sets. Coordinating and recording maintenance belongs here; carrying out the repair belongs to development logistics. Maintaining a building and maintaining the record of who owns it are separate functions, even inside one organisation.

5

Energy resources, sanitation, preservational

Energy resources generates and extracts: power, fuel, mining and forestry, drawing raw supply from the world for direct use as fuel or material. Sanitation decides whether that activity is properly contained and handled, holding it within thresholds of cleanliness, containment and waste handling. Preservational keeps the account of ecological conditions and consequences. A sanitation permit does not make an outcome acceptable. Only the preservational account shows whether it was.

6

Medical, scientific, nutritional provision

Medical agents treat, care and intervene, including in health and fitness. The scientific body approves or denies against established evidence, and a result counts for it only when it holds up to testing and repetition. Nutritional provision records and reviews production, preparation, availability, consumption, diets and requirements: the whole supply of what people take in. Pharmaceuticals divide along the same line: prescribing and administering a drug is medical, and accounting for what people are supplied to consume is nutritional provision. Cooking a meal is an action. Accounting for whether people are actually nourished is the authoritative function.

7

Manufacturing, commercial, financial

Manufacturing produces goods to authorised commercial requirements; read widely, it is the whole system of supply and demand that turns orders into things. Commercial approves or denies proposals, commissions, contracts, loans and commitments. Financial records and reviews accounts, capital, transactions, investments and obligations: the ledgers of banks, the positions of investors and brokers, the assessments of tax authorities. Funding and energy both sustain an operation, yet they remain separate categories: one is an economic relationship and the other is physical capacity.

8

Content creation, media distribution, news journalism

Content creation produces expressive work: performance, entertainment and commentary. Media distribution decides access, hosting, deployment, publication and circulation. Its occupants are platform founders and administrators, network programmers and the people who deploy servers and set the rules of reach. Its approval takes three forms: permission to publish, the decision to recommend or share, and the audience’s acceptance of the claim. News journalism investigates and returns the account. Publishing words or video does not make anyone a journalist. Purpose decides the position.

9

Cultural, educational, religious

Cultural agents carry family, community and everyday social life through homes, workplaces and gatherings. The educational body approves or denies guidance and qualifications against knowledge and competence requirements. It certifies competence; it does not license cultural life. The religious position records and reviews conduct against spiritual and ethical frameworks, ethical frameworks without religion included. It asks whether inherited interpretations still hold, whether practice matched professed principle, and what now needs reconsidering.

Part IV

Five propositions

  1. Acting, permitting and accounting are different questions. No answer to one settles the others.
  2. Functional distinction locates responsibility. A failed proposal, a bad approval, poor execution and a misleading account are different failures with different remedies.
  3. The account must reach someone who can respond. A record that informs no later request, decision, correction or challenge has no corrective power.
  4. Every domain depends on conditions it cannot produce alone. Public authority needs implementation. Implementation needs infrastructure, resources and people. People need health, nourishment, goods and economic coordination. Accountability needs communication and social life.
  5. Connections between domains provide recourse. When one route closes, an account can travel through another body and return as pressure on the first.

Together these make the model more than a list of professions. It is a classification of capabilities joined to an account of how social activity is sustained and made answerable.

The social loop

The nine bodies run in a fixed order, and body 9 returns to body 1.

  1. Governmental activity gives public authority its basis and its accountability.
  2. Legal activity gives claims and disputes an organised means of submission and response.
  3. Enforcement connects authorised decisions to interventions in the world.
  4. Development logistics supplies the planning, infrastructure, maintenance and movement those interventions require.
  5. Energy resources supplies material and energetic capacity.
  6. Medical care and nutritional provision sustain the people doing the work.
  7. Manufacturing, commercial and financial functions handle goods, commitments and the accounting of resources.
  8. Creation, distribution and journalism handle expression, circulation and the public account.
  9. Cultural life is where people meet, contest and live with all of it. Their shared conviction becomes public expectation, and that expectation becomes government’s agenda.

The order descends through authority, access and resources. It runs from the body that frames public power, through the bodies that give that power legal form and practical force, then the material, human, economic and expressive conditions that sustain it, and finally into the everyday life that answers back. The loop is the route authority travels and the route an account travels back.

Dependencies run wider than the loop. Development depends on finance, medicine on logistics, and journalism on people, equipment and power. The loop traces how authority flows, and the network of dependencies shows what each body needs to function. A dependency names a need. It does not certify that the need is met. Funding and energy show why the categories stay apart even where they combine: both drive an operation the way fuel and finance both keep an engine running, and each still has its own triad to account for it.

Reading the loop backwards

The loop also reads in reverse, as evidence. When a story refused by its distributor reaches the public through cultural life and returns as pressure, the link that carried it is alive, and a live link testifies to the bodies behind it. Government is still holding itself to the transparent release of truth. Law is still carrying claims and representing rights in court. Enforcement still has agents in the field gathering what is real and deciding on it. Those agents can still move and plan their operations, and energy still powers them. Each live link is evidence that the bodies it depends on are working. Each broken link shows where to look.

From conviction to agenda

Body 9 closes the loop. A community’s religious and ethical life is the democratic expression of convictions that are hard to consolidate into single claims: what is owed to a neighbour, what honesty requires, what a shared resource means. Those convictions shape what the population expects. The population makes government representative on its behalf, and through participation, advocacy, voting and representation its expectations become government’s agenda, where they are argued into claims and the constitution is tested, rectified or amended in response.

What travels through the loop

The loop carries shared conviction into explicit proposals, carries proposals into practical consequences, and carries those consequences back into public understanding. What moves through it is an interpretation of reality, not reality itself.

“Law” in this model has three registers.

Public lawMade by the stateMade and ruled on by the state.
Canonical lawHeld by a traditionWhat a tradition holds as settled teaching.
Physical lawEstablished by testingThe regularities observation and testing establish: gravity, the speed of light, the results of a screening.

All three enter the same argument: in the water case, test results constrain the claims about the water, ethical commitments define responsibility, and public law sets the remedy. They remain distinct. A ruling settles a question within its authority, but it does not settle physical fact. Religious review has to be able to question its own past readings in the light of evidence, or the review becomes a defence and stops being an account.

New law and new interpretation

A review resolves in one of two ways, and the model keeps them apart. A new interpretation forms inside a tradition: religious review reaffirms an earlier reading, exposes a tension, or reinterprets what a duty requires now, and the tradition’s own process decides whether that reading becomes canonical. A new law forms in the state: the account goes forward as a request, governmental agents draft and submit, and the constitutional body approves or denies. Where a law already exists, legal agents argue it and the judicial body rules.

In the water case both happen. The tradition comes to hold that care for a neighbour includes honesty about shared dangers, and the public asks for a law requiring water-test results to be published. Religious review motivates and informs the legal change; it never enacts it. When review reaffirms an old reading, it explains why the new evidence leaves its commitments intact. When it finds tension, it says so, and returns that tension to community life to be lived with, argued over and changed. Whatever law results stays open to review, and the loop continues.

Part V

Worked case: the contaminated water supply

Residents who share a water supply suspect contamination. The concern forms in bodies 8 and 9 before it ever reaches government.

A resident films the discoloured water and posts the video: content creation, enact and submit. Media distribution lets it circulate, and viewers accept or reject what it claims. Both are approvals, and rejection still spreads it. News journalism checks the claim, tests the evidence and returns a fuller account. That account enters cultural life through families, workplaces and neighbours, and a community meeting is called to request precautions. At the meeting the educational body endorses or rejects the proposed guidance, and an informed speaker explains the grounds.

Religious review then asks how the response fits the community’s inherited understanding of reality, truth and its obligations to others. It returns a shared conviction: protecting our neighbours requires honest disclosure of dangers to the water we share. Through participation, advocacy, voting and representation, that conviction becomes a demand on government. Religious communities contribute alongside every other community and citizen. The conviction carries weight because it is shared, not because one community speaks for everyone.

The same person moves through several positions in that sequence. The resident who filmed the water is a creator, then an audience member, then a voice at the meeting. The positions do not merge because she occupies them in turn. From there the concern travels the whole loop.

Worked case: the blocked story

A journalist holds an evidenced account of an over-budget bridge contract, and the main media distributor refuses to carry it. The model shows where the account goes next.

StepBodyWhat happens
18Media distribution refuses publication.
29The account enters cultural circulation through conversation, community discussion, public gatherings and independent sharing.
39An informed speaker explains it, and the community reviews it against its shared commitments.
41Public concern becomes pressure on government, and the response is checked constitutionally.
52A records request and a ruling compel disclosure, and auditorial reviews the process.
67The disclosed records are set against the original commercial approval and the financial account.

A refusal in one domain does not end the matter while another legitimate route remains. That is the purpose of the descending order: a distributor holds a veto over its own channel and over nothing else. Two conditions govern that route:

  • The route must be genuinely open. If the same gatekeeper controls the alternative channel, renaming it creates no new path.
  • Circulation is not truth. A true account and a false rumour can both spread. The route guarantees a hearing, and evidence and review decide the claim.

Building on the model

The structure is set. The next stage of construction fills in the operating rules:

  • A cannot-do list for every triad, built to the standard auditorial already meets.
  • Who occupies each authorising position, and where its remit ends.
  • What makes an account independent enough and open enough to challenge.
  • How conflicting approvals or accounts are resolved.
  • Further routes of recourse, beyond the journalism-to-culture route.
  • Cases that cross several domains at once. A bank collapse is the next case to run through the loop.
Part VI

Three ways to position them

Part VI places bodies 2 to 9 on the eight corners of a cube. Each body receives a three-bit code that records how each of its positions stands toward the person in front of it. The cube then shows which complete routes through society are possible when one relationship changes at a time.

NotationMeaning
E, B, AEmbodied agent, authoritative body, authoritative agent
CodeThree bits read left to right as E-B-A, for example 101
RouteAn ordered path through all eight codes that changes one bit per step and returns to its start
PulseThe position whose bit changes four times in a route, on alternating steps
Collective nameThe name of a code, carried by whichever body occupies it

The bit

A 1 marks a relationship in focus, at high resolution. It runs both ways on equal terms: your influence over the position stands in balanced proportion to your will, and the pathway is open for transformative change between you. A 0 marks a relationship out of focus: it runs one way, or returns on unequal terms. A 1 requires both conditions, so influence that flows both ways but unequally scores 0. Every code is read from the position of the individual person.

BitPositionA 1 meansExample
EEmbodied agentWhat can be done to you, you can also have doneYou can call the police, and the police can be called on you
BAuthoritative bodyWhat is decided about you, you can reachA judgment about you, or the knowledge record of what you did
AAuthoritative agentWhat records you, you can see and reviewA record of your actions that includes you

A 0 does not mean that a position is absent or that contact with it is forbidden. A 1 does not mean unlimited access. The code measures standing, not presence.

A collective reads some bodies differently from a person. One resident cannot move the preservational account of a river; an organised environmental movement can. The cube records the individual reading. The collective reading is a second register, scored by the same rule.

Body 1 is the bridge. The governmental triad describes the system as a whole, not a function inside it, so it is not a corner. It carries the loop from body 9 back to body 2, and it has its own reading, set out below under the top row.

  • Legal (101). Your advocate argues with you and for you, and the cross-examination of the record runs back and forth with you. The judge is the one position that does not answer back.
  • Enforcement (111). The police are the public face of the triad: you can call them, and they can be called on you. Intelligence, read as a knowledge record, holds you as much as your actions put out, and the copy is one you can reach. Surveillance mirrors the camera: the record is equal to the act. All three stand level with you.
  • Development logistics (011). The builders answer to the companies that commission them, not to you. Civic welfare hears you through consultation and objection, and the record of what you own is yours to check.
  • Energy resources (010). Read from the individual, you cannot supply the grid as it supplies you, and the account of its environmental cost is not yours to review. Only sanitation meets you on equal terms, through the consumer relationship and the hygiene of your own home and surroundings.
  • Medical (110). Doctors meet you on equal terms, and so does the scientific side: you take part in studies, consent or refuse, and speak with the researchers. The nutritional account of what farmers and producers supply is not one you stand level with.
  • Manufacturing (100). You can make as well as buy, and as a consumer you steer supply and demand. The commercial decision is not yours to reach, and the financial account kept of you is not one you review on equal terms.
  • Content creation (000). Anyone can post, dispute and share. Posting is influence, but not equal influence over what is distributed, so all three positions score 0. That is the reason this is the transmissible corner: material moves through it without anyone standing level with the system that moves it.
  • Cultural (001). The religious account is the one you enter on equal terms: the review of conduct against principle includes you and answers you. Everyday social life and educational approval act on you before you can act on them.

The cube and its routes

The cube has 8 corners, 12 edges and exactly 6 routes that visit every corner once while changing one bit per step. Each route has a pulse: one position changes four times and the other two change twice each. There are three pulse families, one for each position.

Every way keeps two anchors: legal at 101 and enforcement at 111. Four of the six routes contain that edge. Three of them form the three ways, one from each pulse family. The fourth is a second route in the authoritative-body family.

Way one: the embodied agent leads

Route 101 → 111 → 011 → 010 → 110 → 100 → 000 → 001 → 101. Pulse: E (steps B, E, A, E, B, E, A, E).

Way two: the authoritative body leads

Route 101 → 111 → 110 → 100 → 000 → 010 → 011 → 001 → 101. Pulse: B (steps B, A, B, E, B, A, B, E).

Rows 2 to 4 are scored. Judicial and intelligence fit. Civic welfare fits at 110 when it is read as population health: the welfare decision and the builders meet you on equal terms, while the property record does not. Rows 5 to 9 are next, starting with medical at 000.

Way three: the authoritative agent leads

Route 101 → 111 → 110 → 010 → 011 → 001 → 000 → 100 → 101. Pulse: A (steps B, A, E, A, B, A, E, A).

The route closes from 100 back to 101 by changing the account bit, so the return passes through diplomatic, the account position of body 1. Rows 4 to 9 are next.

The names belong to the codes, not the bodies. In ways two and three, development logistics sits at 110, so it takes Reproducible. Each name describes a quality of authority at its corner, and Environmental is the one that also names a domain; it became free for corner 010 when the account position of body 5 was renamed Preservational. The names were chosen for way one, and each other way tests whether a name still describes the body that inherits it.

The top row

Body 1 is read on the same three positions but asks a different question: does each position hold greater or lesser influence than the individual? The reciprocity reading asks whether a relationship is equal. The top row reads the system itself, where equality is never the starting point. The model runs on one cube with two readings: equal or unequal for bodies 2 to 9, greater or lesser for body 1.

PositionThe question
GovernmentalDo you nominate it, or is it appointed over you?
ConstitutionalCan you amend what binds you, or only obey it?
DiplomaticAre you fairly represented, and free to oppose the one who represents you?

The governmental row is not fixed to one corner. It can sit at any of the eight, and where it sits names the kind of regime in place.

The top row is the newest layer of the model. Four tasks complete it: naming the eight regime types, marking equal and unknown influence, deciding whether the collective names carry over, and defining the path a regime travels from one corner to another.

How unlikely the fit is

Assignments40,320Ways to assign eight codes to eight bodies.
Close into a route1 in 42096 of them close into a one-bit route.
With the anchors fixed1 in 1804 of the remaining 720 close.

The one-bit rule was spoken aloud while legal and enforcement were being scored, so those two rows count as anchors. With them fixed, 4 of the remaining 720 assignments close: 1 in 180. That is the measure of how unlikely it is for the remaining six rows to land on a route by chance.

Testing the positions

  1. Record the predictions first. Write the expected code for every body on every way before anyone else scores them.
  2. Use blind raters. Give them the bit and the position definitions, but not the codes, the cube or the one-bit rule.
  3. Use human raters. Separate AI instances share training and agree with each other too readily.
  4. Report agreement row by row, alongside every point of divergence.
  5. Run a case built to strain the model. A bank collapse comes first.

How the model was built

The structure came first and the cube came last.

  1. Seed domains. About 15 to 20 domains named from memory: religion, family, education, government, media, arts and entertainment, business, legal, financial, cultural, medical, technological, surveillance, political, transport, food production, manufacturing and agriculture.
  2. Expansion. A thirty-row table of societal domains, with “institutional” set aside as an umbrella term.
  3. Comparison. Parsons’ AGIL model, PESTLE, the security sectors of Buzan, Wæver and de Wilde, and the UNDP dimensions of human security. All four classify domains, and none separates capabilities into triples. Parsons derives four functions from two yes-or-no questions; this model derives eight corners from three, and places a separation of capabilities inside every domain.
  4. Triads. Surveillance, intelligence and enforcement first, then legal, judicial and auditorial, and the rest by the same separation test, giving 27 components in nine triads.
  5. Positions. Enact and submit, approve or deny, record and review, fixed by meaning.
  6. Cube. Three-bit codes scored row by row against the finished structure.

A few common ones, Talcott Parsons's AGIL model. It compresses society into four essential functions. Adaptation, goal attainment, integration, and pattern maintenance. Think economy, government, community and law, and institutions like family, education, and religion. PESTLE is another. Political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental. Used a lot in strategic analysis of countries and organizations. For a geopolitical frame, Buzan, Wæver, and de Wilde talk about five security sectors. Military, political, economic, societal, and environmental. UNDP's seven dimensions of human security is another. Economic, food, health, environmental, personal, community, and political. If you mean 'what makes society function,' start with Parsons. If you want broad category headings, PESTLE. If you want power, threats, and stability, Buzan and colleagues.

Approving a loan is its commercial function. Maintaining and reviewing the account of balances, obligations, and repayments is its financial function. The institution contains both, but that does not make those capabilities identical. The same principle applies elsewhere. A journalist can create entertainment; a creator can investigate a public claim. Their position depends on the activity being performed. Your three roles therefore remain: Role Agreed capability Central question Individual agent Enacts and submits; responds and requests. What is being proposed, attempted, or carried out? Authoritative body Approves or denies. May this proceed under the applicable requirements? Authoritative agent Records and reviews, returning an account. What occurred, what conditions apply, and how does the activity compare? “Individual agent” identifies the acting position; it need not imply that every operation is performed by one solitary person. The authoritative agent’s account also need not wait until an action has finished. Existing records and current conditions can inform a request, an approval, an ongoing intervention, or a later review. A compact expression is: An agent acts or requests; a body authorises or denies; an authoritative agent records and reviews. The returned account informs what happens next. That is the recurring relationship. It does not require every interaction to follow an inflexible three-step timetable. The nine triads, in your agreed order The terms remain within your one-to-two-word limit. The definitions describe their assigned functions in your model. # Individual agent — enact/submit; respond/request Authoritative body — approve/deny Authoritative agent — record/review 1 Governmental — Carries out public administration, policy, and military defence. Constitutional — Approves or denies governmental proposals against constitutional requirements. Diplomatic — Records and reviews national relations, commitments, and external conditions. 2 Legal — Develops arguments, submits applications, and responds to decisions. Judicial — Approves or denies applications through authoritative legal rulings. Auditorial — Independently records and reviews authorised material, procedures, and outcomes. 3 Enforcement — Requests operational permission and carries out authorised interventions. Intelligence — Assesses information and approves or denies proposed operations. Surveillance — Records and reviews observations through separately controlled monitoring infrastructure. 4 Development logistics — Designs, plans, builds, maintains, and moves people and goods. Civic welfare — Approves or denies proposals against community requirements. Property stewardship — Records and reviews ownership, tenure, possessions, and asset responsibilities. 5 Energy resources — Carries out energy generation, extraction, mining, and forestry. Sanitation — Approves or denies operations against sanitation and containment requirements. Environmental — Records and reviews environmental conditions, impacts, and reported outcomes. 6 Medical — Provides treatment, care, and health and fitness interventions. Scientific — Approves or denies proposals against established scientific requirements. Nutritional provision — Records and reviews food production, preparation, consumption, and requirements. 7 Manufacturing — Produces goods in response to authorised commercial requirements. Commercial — Approves or denies business proposals, commissions, and commitments. Financial — Records and reviews accounts, capital, transactions, and obligations. 8 Content creation — Produces expressive works, entertainment, performances, and other creative material. Media distribution — Approves or denies access, hosting, publication, and distribution. News journalism — Records, investigates, and reviews events, claims, and public consequences. 9 Socio-cultural — Enacts family, community, cultural, and everyday social life. Educational — Approves or denies qualifications against knowledge and competence requirements. Religious — Records and reviews conduct against spiritual and ethical frameworks. These are your proposed functional assignments, not descriptions of a universally existing institutional arrangement. Why the refinements matter Several of your corrections made the framework substantially more precise. Development logistics includes architecture, design, planning proposals, construction, maintenance, and movement. Transport is one expression of that capability. Its broader function is to organise and carry out changes in the material world. Property stewardship supplies the corresponding account of rights and responsibilities. It covers land, buildings, tenure, district and location records, personal possessions, ownership claims, use rights, and asset condition. Maintaining a building and maintaining the account of who owns it are distinguishable functions, even when one organisation handles both. Sanitation, in your explanation, concerns whether energy and resource activity is appropriately contained and responsibly handled. Environmental supplies the wider account of the conditions and consequences through which that responsibility can be assessed. A sanitation approval and an environmental outcome remain different things: permission does not establish that the resulting conditions were acceptable. Nutritional provision extends beyond farming to production, preparation, availability, consumption, diets, and nutritional requirements. Its position concerns the recorded and reviewed conditions of nourishment. Producing a meal remains an action; the authoritative function is accounting for provision and its relationship to requirements. You did not settle on pharmaceuticals as the umbrella label, and this synthesis does not reinstate it. Financial covers accounts, capital, transactions, obligations, investment positions, and related records. Your bank example resolves the apparent overlap: financial accounting and commercial approval can coexist within one institution while remaining separate functions. Content creation, media distribution, and news journalism distinguishes producing expression, deciding its distribution, and investigating or reporting an account. The distinction follows the purpose and function of the activity, rather than treating everyone who publishes words or video as performing the same role. How the nine rows connect The rows are not nine self-contained compartments. Your explanation gives them a relationship of practical dependence and returning scrutiny: 1. Governmental activity needs a basis for public authority and accountability. 2. Legal activity gives claims and disputes an organised means of submission and response. 3. Enforcement connects authorised decisions with interventions in the world. 4. Development logistics supplies the planning, infrastructure, maintenance, and movement those interventions require. 5. Energy resources supplies material and energetic capacity for operations. 6. Medical activity and nutritional provision concern the health and nourishment of the people sustaining those operations. 7. Manufacturing, commercial, and financial functions concern goods, commitments, and the accounting of economic resources. 8. Creation, distribution, and journalism concern expression, circulation, and public accounts. 9. Socio-cultural life is where people encounter, discuss, adopt, contest, and live with those activities and accounts. Community experience and public scrutiny can then feed back into government, claims, and subsequent decisions. That last connection makes the sequence capable of forming a cycle. However, the ordering need not imply that every dependency travels only to the next row. Development also depends on finance; medical activity depends on logistics; journalism depends on people, equipment, and energy. The nine-row sequence organises the explanation, while the actual dependencies form a network. Likewise, funding and energy can both sustain an operation without becoming the same category. Funding belongs to its commercial and financial relationships; energy supplies physical capacity. Your engine metaphor connects them without requiring their functions to collapse together. The journalism-to-community connection Your most important clarification was that journalism has a potential route into socio-cultural circulation when formal media distribution refuses publication. An account may be carried through conversation, community discussion, public gatherings, independent sharing, or other accessible channels. A story can become a public concern or trend without first receiving approval from one particular distributor. Within your framework, that creates a route of recourse across domains: A blocked journalistic account can enter community circulation and potentially return as public pressure, a legal claim, or a demand for governmental response. This changes the assessment of the eighth triad. Examining media distribution in isolation misses the alternative route you intended through the ninth. The precise qualification is accessibility: the community route must actually be usable. If the same gatekeeper controls it too, its alternative name does not create an alternative path. Circulation also does not itself establish truth. A truthful account and a false rumour can both become trends. The route preserves the possibility of being heard; investigation, evidence, and review remain necessary for assessing the claim. The coherent rationale for the whole The framework can be understood through five connected propositions. First, acting, permitting, and accounting answer different questions.An action demonstrates that something happened. An approval establishes that a designated body permitted it. A reviewed account supplies information about the conditions, process, and consequences. None automatically substitutes for the other two. Second, functional distinction makes responsibility easier to locate.When an operation fails, the model helps distinguish an inadequate proposal, an unjustified approval, poor execution, and an incomplete or misleading account. Several can occur together, but they are different failures requiring different responses. Third, the account must remain capable of informing subsequent activity.Records that cannot reach anyone able to respond have limited corrective value. The returning relationship matters: review informs further requests, decisions, corrections, or challenges. Fourth, every domain depends on conditions it cannot produce alone.Public authority requires practical implementation. Implementation requires infrastructure, resources, and people. Sustaining those people requires health, nourishment, goods, and economic coordination. Public accountability requires communication and social engagement. The domains remain mutually dependent despite their different responsibilities. Fifth, connections between domains can provide recourse when a local process fails.Your journalism-to-community example demonstrates this principle. A refusal in one domain need not end the matter if another legitimate route remains available. That is the basis for investigating further routes of recourse elsewhere in the framework; those additional routes have not yet all been agreed. Together, these propositions explain why the framework is more than a list of professions. It combines a classification of capabilities with a proposed account of how social activity is sustained and made answerable. What is established, and what remains to be demonstrated The conversation establishes: ● The three capabilities and their recurring relationship. ● The nine-triad order and the refined category names. ● Classification by function, including multiple functions within one institution. ● Practical interdependence between domains. ● Socio-cultural circulation as a potential recourse for blocked journalism. Further design work would need to establish: ● Who occupies each authorising position and the limits of their remit. ● What makes an account sufficiently independent and open to challenge. ● How conflicting approvals or accounts are resolved. ● Which alternative routes exist beyond the journalism example. ● How the model handles cases that cross several domains at once. These are implementation questions rather than reasons to abandon the structure. But they matter to the strength of its claims. In particular, an active journalism-to-community link can support accountability; it does not by itself prove that government is democratic, rights are protected, or every other domain functions properly. Similarly, showing that an operation requires energy, logistics, or finance identifies necessary support—not proof that adequate support exists. The nine domains provide a coherent proposed organisation. Their completeness and optimality would require testing against concrete cases rather than being established by the symmetry of the table. The combined working explanation The Nine-Domain Accountability Cycle organises social activity through three recurring capabilities: the individual agent enacts and submits, or responds and requests; the authoritative body approves or denies; and the authoritative agent records and reviews, returning an account that can inform subsequent action and authorisation. These capabilities classify functions. A single institution may perform several, but its actions, permissions, and accounts remain distinguishable. This makes it possible to ask who acted, who authorised the action, what was recorded, and how the resulting account can be questioned or used. The structure repeats across nine ordered domains, extending from governmental and constitutional relationships through law, enforcement, development, resources, health, production, communication, and socio-cultural life. Each domain relies on material, human, informational, or institutional conditions supplied by others. Accountability therefore operates both within and between domains. Within a triad, action and authorisation remain subject to a returned account. Between domains, information, dependencies, and routes of recourse connect the process to wider social life. Journalism’s potential movement into community circulation when formal distribution is blocked illustrates this connection. The framework’s purpose is to make those relationships explicit: what enables activity, what permits it, what accounts for it, and where a response remains possible when a particular route fails. Its success depends on whether those distinctions and connections work in practice.

Yes—the connection you’re describing is that a community’s religious life expresses shared understandings of reality, truth, and responsibility; those understandings help shape the population’s expectations; and representative government gives those expectations a form that can be proposed, considered, and acted upon. A collective conviction can exist before anyone has consolidated it into a specific claim. In The Nine Bodies of Authority, each triad gives that process three distinguishable positions: ● Embodied agent: enacts and submits; responds and requests. ● Authoritative body: approves or denies. ● Authoritative agent: records and reviews, returning an account. Here is the full loop, using the water-contamination example and your agreed order. These are the functions assigned within your model. The return from religious review into government The water concern has already travelled through public discussion, a community meeting, and educational guidance. Religious review now considers how the response fits the community’s inherited understanding of Creator, reality, truth, and obligations to others. That review might produce a shared conviction: “Protecting our neighbours requires honest disclosure of dangers to the water we share.” People may agree on that responsibility while disagreeing about its exact interpretation or implementation. Through participation, advocacy, voting, and representation, those convictions inform what people ask government to do. Religious communities contribute to this process alongside other communities and nonreligious citizens. A religious community can express part of the public’s convictions; it does not automatically constitute the majority or speak for everyone. Your connection works without requiring that equivalence. 1. Governmental → Constitutional → Diplomatic Governmental embodied agents consolidate public concerns into a proposed collective response: investigate the water supply, coordinate assistance, and propose clearer disclosure requirements. The constitutional authoritative body considers whether that response fits the foundational distribution of powers and protections. Within your model, it approves or denies the proposal on that basis. A conflict could prompt revision of the proposal, reconsideration of an interpretation, or a proposal to amend the constitutional framework. Amendment would be a distinct process, rather than an automatic consequence of public agreement. The diplomatic authoritative agent records and reviews the response against external relationships, commitments, and conditions—for example, where a water source crosses borders or responsibility involves neighbouring jurisdictions. What passes forward: a publicly proposed response, its constitutional standing, and an account of its wider relationships. 2. Legal → Judicial → Auditorial Legal embodied agents formulate specific claims, arguments, applications, and responses: what responsibility was owed, what evidence supports a breach, and what remedy is sought. The judicial authoritative body approves or denies applications and determines contested claims within its remit. The auditorial authoritative agent records and reviews the evidence presented, procedures followed, reasoning supplied, and resulting decisions. Your broader concern with “laws of reality” enters here through the premises and evidence used in an argument. Physical findings, inherited principles, and recognised obligations need to be represented accurately, while remaining distinguishable. A ruling settles a question within its authority; it does not determine physical reality itself. What passes forward: a defined basis for action, together with an account of how that basis was established. 3. Enforcement → Intelligence → Surveillance Enforcement embodied agents request and carry out interventions: inspect a suspected discharge site, secure relevant evidence, or implement an authorised restriction. The intelligence authoritative body, in your assignment, assesses available information and approves or denies proposed operations within the permissions established above. The surveillance authoritative agent records and reviews observations and operational activity: what was found, what occurred, and whether subsequent conditions match the account provided. What passes forward: an operational account of the problem and the practical requirements for addressing it. What passes forward: an operational account of the problem and the practical requirements for addressing it. 4. Development logistics → Civic welfare → Property stewardship Development logistics embodied agents design and submit practical plans: repair a pipe, establish temporary water access, move equipment, and organise maintenance. The civic welfare authoritative body approves or denies proposals against community requirements, including access, disruption, and the needs of affected residents. The property stewardship authoritative agent records and reviews ownership, tenure, access rights, asset conditions, and responsibilities for the infrastructure involved. What passes forward: an assessed plan identifying what must be built, moved, maintained, or accessed, and who holds the relevant responsibilities. 5. Energy resources → Sanitation → Environmental Energy resources embodied agents propose and supply the energy and raw materials needed for the work: power for pumps, fuel for transport, and resources for replacement infrastructure. The sanitation authoritative body approves or denies proposed operations against containment, cleanliness, and waste-handling requirements within your model. The environmental authoritative agent records and reviews ecological conditions and consequences: whether contamination persists, whether remediation helps, and whether the work introduces further damage. What passes forward: an account of the material support supplied and its environmental consequences. 6. Medical → Scientific → Nutritional provision Medical embodied agents respond to possible health effects, provide care, and propose appropriate interventions. The scientific authoritative body assesses those proposals against relevant evidence and scientific requirements, approving or denying them within its assigned remit. The nutritional provision authoritative agent records and reviews conditions of nourishment: access to safe drinking water, effects on food preparation, availability of alternatives, and whether people’s requirements are being met. What passes forward: an account of health responses and the conditions necessary to sustain the affected population. 7. Manufacturing → Commercial → Financial Manufacturing embodied agents produce required goods: replacement pipes, containers, treatment equipment, and other supplies. The commercial authoritative body approves or denies commissions, purchases, contracts, and business commitments. The financial authoritative agent records and reviews accounts, capital, payments, debts, and obligations. Your bank distinction applies directly: deciding whether to extend a loan occupies the commercial position; maintaining and reviewing the financial account occupies the financial position. What passes forward: goods, commercial commitments, and a reviewable account of how resources were funded and used. 8. Content creation → Media distribution → News journalism Content creation embodied agents turn these experiences and outcomes into public expression: a resident’s update, an explanatory video, a documentary, or a critique of the response. Media distribution includes decisions about publication and circulation, together with the participating audience’s acceptance or rejection of the proposition. Those are distinguishable forms of approval: permission to publish, decisions to recommend or share, and agreement with the claim. The news journalism authoritative agent records, investigates, and reviews the emerging account: whether repairs occurred, what the tests show, how money was spent, and whether official promises match observed outcomes. What passes forward: a public account that people can encounter, question, discuss, and answer. 9. Socio-cultural → Educational → Religious Socio-cultural embodied agents carry the account into everyday life through families, workplaces, conversations, gatherings, and community organising. They respond and make further requests. The educational authoritative body, in your broader usage, considers and endorses or rejects proposed guidance. A community meeting, informed speaker, or public explanation helps people understand the grounds for that guidance. The religious authoritative agent records and reviews how the experience relates to inherited faith, understandings of reality, and ethical commitments. It asks whether previous interpretations remain coherent, whether conduct lived up to professed principles, and what now requires reconsideration. That returned understanding influences community conduct and the expectations people bring to their representatives. The loop returns to governmental activity. The complete order is therefore: Body Embodied agent Authoritative body Authoritative agent 1 Governmental Constitutional Diplomatic 2 Legal Judicial Auditorial 3 Enforcement Intelligence Surveillance 4 Development logistics Civic welfare Property stewardship 5 Energy resources Sanitation Environmental 6 Medical Scientific Nutritional provision 7 Manufacturing Commercial Financial 8 Content creation Media distribution News journalism 9 Socio-cultural Educational Religious What holds the loop together is the movement from shared conviction into explicit proposals, from proposals into practical consequences, and from those consequences back into public understanding and renewed conviction. The order gives you a coherent way to trace that movement. Actual activity also crosses between rows: healthcare may be needed immediately, finance supports earlier operations, and journalism can scrutinise any stage. So the strongest version of your framework treats the sequence as a recurring route through connected responsibilities, with each returned account capable of changing what happens next.

How to read this page

Solid means settled, selected, or travelled. Dashed means computed, contingent, needs work, or uncertain; mark uncertainty with [?]. Dotted means held, unexplored, a possible path not taken, or a cannot-do (a held, unexercised power). One focal line marks the one thing being read.

Line grammarA key to the line grammar. Solid is settled, selected, or travelled. Dashed is computed, contingent, needs work, or uncertain; mark uncertainty with [?]. Dotted is held, unexplored, a possible path not taken, or a cannot-do (held power, unexercised). The focal label names the current position, one per view. It is text only, not a second focal mark; the keyboard-focus-ring exception is not used for this legend.
